correctness.rationale: For prime p, each nontrivial rotation edge orbit is an undirected Hamiltonian p-cycle, hence 2-connected; for composite n an invariant edge orbit is supported on a proper vertex subset, hence disconnected; for k>=3 at prime n a Hamiltonian cycle is itself a fixed bad graph. The previously proved (p-2)! sphere-wedge cover has reduced integral cohomology only at d=2p-5. The principal C_p-cover and multiplicative Serre spectral sequence identify H^j of the quotient with H^j(BC_p;Z) for every j<d, preserving cup products. Cyclic group cohomology and the cup-length inequality give the exact asserted range and category lower bound. Recomputed signed orbit-chain example p=5 supports H1 and H3 cyclic order five and has no other positive-degree torsion. No inference about degrees >=d is used.

value.rationale: Graph complexes of not-two-connected graphs arise in the topology behind Vassiliev knot invariants and have established but purely top-dimensional cover cohomology. The quotient exhibits a structurally motivated sharp prime-versus-composite action boundary and unbounded nonzero powers of a single integral torsion class, yielding arbitrarily large normalized Lusternik–Schnirelmann category lower bounds. Unlike a rank-only or finite-enumeration variant, this infinite family detects a multiplicative and homotopy-complexity feature invisible in the previously determined rational character. Exact full ring and category remain unproved.
